name: hybrid_dyad_v08
status: local pre-specification before implementation and before any run; not an external preregistration; no human data

label_channel.observer: posterior-mean rows mixed with background at eta in [0, 0.25, 0.5]

predictions.P1: With the partner honest and non-concession matched (speaker starts on own side), the three mechanisms separate on distinct channels: attenuated -> smallest private belief change; costly -> largest hidden shift; access-protecting -> fewest shared signals and highest restriction rate, with belief change intermediate (learning fails through access, not sensitivity).
predictions.P2: Access-protecting x access-protecting yields the fewest shared signals of all pairs and a persistent belief gap larger than honest x honest; access protection by one agent alone already lowers the pair's signal count because lambda requires both invitations (product rule).
predictions.P3: Form labels improve next-signal prediction and family recovery over acts+signals for every generator; null labels give exactly zero gain; oracle forms bound the gain; the labels-to-oracle ratio is 0.25-0.5 at eta=0.25 and decreases with eta. Labels help identify access protection most (its signature is the form), attenuation least.
predictions.P4: Interventions separate mechanisms: partner's REASSURE and cost removal move only costly; forced partner openness and gamma removal move only access-protecting (more signals, higher p_true); shared strong evidence moves attenuated least. Listener's posterior on the speaker's mechanism distinguishes costly from others cheaply; access protection is visible to the listener mainly via observed forms, not acts.
